preamble: Raising of the close-mid back unrounded vowel [ɤ] to the close [ɯ]. Pittayaporn (2009) reconstructs Proto-Tai long *ɤː, which in open syllables was raised and merged with *ɯː in Southwestern and Central Tai, including Siamese (Thai), Lao, Lungchow, Lungming, Debao and Jingxi: *zɤːᴮ 'straight' became Siamese sɯː and Lungchow ɬɯː. All Northern Tai dialects and a few Central Tai varieties rounded it to o instead (Yay θo), and Qinzhou lowered it to aː. In closed syllables *ɤː diphthongized to ɯə in Siamese (*rɤːnᴬ 'house' > Siamese rɯən); Lungchow has ɤː there, from earlier *ɯə. Pittayaporn notes that only a handful of etyma with open-syllable *ɤː are known.

examples.to: ซื่อ sɯː (tone B2) 'honest, straightforward'

examples.note: Yay has θo and so for these two words.
